Rock band from Burnage, Manchester, formed in 1991 out of the ashes of a band called The Rain (consisting of [a605785], [a605786], [a429260] and Chris Hutton on vocals) who started in 1990. Chris was sacked and [a53887] took over on vocals. His brother [a5452] (former guitar roadie for [a=Inspiral Carpets]' [a=Clint Boon]) then joined as songwriter and additional guitarist.
In 1999, two of the founding members (Guigsy and Bonehead) left the group and Noel played their parts on the fourth album. Two new musicians were recruited - [a447669] and [a80566] - initially for touring duties, but became full-time and were part of the songwriting process on the following albums.  
On August 28, 2009, Noel announced that he was leaving the band after an altercation with Liam. The remaining members continued performing as [a=Beady Eye] before splitting up in 2014 while Noel formed [a2384642]. 
On 27 August 2024, Oasis announced that they would reform for live performances in 2025.
Short after this announcement their record company re-released some of their work (e.g. 30th anniversary edition "Definitely Maybe", 7"-Boxes, ...).

profile.profile:
One of the second wave of influential Chicago house producers and a member of the vanguard of late-'90s American house producers, DJ Sneak wasn't born in the Windy City but began listening to house soon after his family arrived from Puerto Rico in the early '80s. Because he couldn't speak English, Sneak gravitated to instrumental music (as well as graffiti art), and became inspired by Chicago legends such as [a=Marshall Jefferson] and [a=DJ Pierre]. Many of those early innovators had left Chicago for the East Coast by the late '80s, when Sneak was ready to start in the business; by 1992, however, [a=Cajmere] had begun a resurgence in the city's classic sound by starting up [l=Cajual Records]. Sneak aided in the revolution with a series of singles on Cajual's sister label, the harder-oriented [l=Relief Records]. Besides other productions for Strictly Rhythm, Henry St., ZYX, 83 West and Feverpitch (several of which feature [a=Armand Van Helden] on co-production, building on the Latin vibes of their heritage), DJ Sneak has also released mix compilations including 1996's Kinky Trax Collection and the following year's Buggin' Da Beats. He also worked in the Gramophone Records store in Chicago.

Founder of the independent vinyl labels [l=Defiant] (1993), [l=Magnetic] (2001) and [l=Oomph] (2002) as well as [l=Leg] (1995) for promo releases plus digital only labels [l=Sneaks House] (2008) and [l=Sneak Tip Music] (2008).

In 1995 he established his own record store called "Sneak Beats" in Toronto (Canada) which sold underground house music on Vinyl and CDs from their store and by mail order. It closed down approximately 10 years later.
English DJ duo consisting of Tommy (from Kent, England) and Jammo (from High Wycombe, England). Now based out of Bristol.  Influenced by Drum and bass, Dubstep, UK garage and Grime.

Eisuke Mori a.k.a Gnyonpix is from Kyoto. He started his career in mod scene in 1990s. After a blank, he began making dance oriented music. In early 2010s, he encountered with DJ Fulltono. Since then, his style has been Juke/Footwork.From middle of 2020, he has been releases extremely short Juke/Footwork tracks on weekly basis.

Naples-based music producer and DJ selector, he’s the mastermind behind [l=Periodica Records] and [l=Futuribile] - a record club that has become a go-to hub for connoisseurs of rare Italian and Neapolitan sounds from the '70s and '80s.

His journey into music production began during his university years when, as a self-taught artist, he delved into electronic music composition using Cubase. Since 2009, he’s been releasing tracks under various aliases and across multiple labels. In 2015, he launched both Periodica Records and Futuribile, marking a significant turning point in his career and artistic growth. During this period, his collaborations with Raffaele Arcella (Whodamanny) and Enrico Fierro (Milord) flourished, forming a tight-knit production team and building a catalog known for its unique sound and aesthetic signature. As both an artistic and executive producer, he manages not only the musical aspects but also the visual identity of each release. He introduces fresh artistic projects and oversees the Futuribile catalog, with a particular focus on rediscovering and reissuing rare records from the Naples and Italian music scenes.

In 2018, he dropped his debut solo album Night of Cheetah, followed by the Q-disc Jurakan in 2019. Over the years, his sound has evolved, blending influences from Italo-Disco, New Wave, Reggae, and Soft Rock. His 2022 mini LP Deviant Disco marked an important step in his career, earning critical acclaim and landing among the top 50 best-sellers on Discogs that year. Some of his tracks were also featured in campaigns by JBL (USA) and Camper (Spain).

American house and techno group formed in Detroit in 1988. The group was originally composed of producer and composer Kevin Saunderson and Chicago native Shanna Jackson, a.k.a. [a=Paris Grey]. Kevin Saunderson is renowned as one of the Belleville Three (along with [a=Juan Atkins] and [a=Derrick May]), the main originators of the Detroit Techno sound.
[a=Ann Saunderson] (Kevin's wife) has also been involved in the group. 
The group is currently Kevin, [a=Dantiez Saunderson] (their son), and vocalist [a=Steffanie Christian].

Face Invada is an Australian Producer & DJ who has spent much of the past 10 years travelling around Australia, Europe and the UK playing at Clubs, Festivals and Bush Doofs.

With a handful of releases under his belt on labels like Sequel One Records (Poland) Delta9 (Germany) Fresh Recordings(Austria) Waking Life (New Zealand) & The Tech Collective (Australia) he is slowly but surely spreading his sounds around the globe.

Dabbling in Drum & Bass, Footwork and Dubstep his style is both a combination of driving and melodic while remaining technical and minimalist.
Melbourne based producer & DJ, releasing multi genre bass music

Tramar Dillard (born December 16, 1979), better known by his stage name Flo Rida (pronounced  /floʊ ˈɹaɪdə/, "flow rider"), is an American rapper and singer-songwriter. He released his debut album, Mail on Sunday, in March 2008. His debut single "Low", featuring T-Pain, was a No. 1 hit for ten weeks in United States in early 2008. Two other singles resulted from Mail on Sunday: "Elevator" and "In the Ayer". In 2009, his second album R.O.O.T.S. was released; its most successful single "Right Round" was at the top of the Hot 100 for six weeks. Since then, he has released his third studio album titled Only One Flo (Part 1), and his fourth titled Wild Ones.

Island Records (often using a logo that omits "Records") was named for [i]Island In The Sun[/i] (a novel, film, and [a=Harry Belafonte] calypso hit), and was founded in Jamaica in 1959 by [a=Chris Blackwell], [a570526] and [a282882]. In May 1962, Blackwell relocated the label to the UK in order to market music by Jamaican artists to immigrant communities in London and Birmingham. In 1967, however, Island shifted its focus to relatively edgy rock music, and most of its Jamaican acts were moved to the spinoff label [l=Trojan Records]. Island resumed its support of reggae artists with the signing of [a=The Wailers] in 1972.

In the UK, Island was independently distributed until mid-1977 when Blackwell did a deal with [l=EMI Records Ltd.]. The EMI Records Ltd. name thereafter appeared on UK labels until the early 1980s.

For several years, Island licensed American rights to its material to a variety of labels, most frequently  [url=http://www.discogs.com/label/A%26M+Records]A&M[/url] and [url=http://www.discogs.com/label/Atlantic]Atlantic[/url]. In 1971, Island first gained its own US label identity through a distribution deal with [url=http://www.discogs.com/label/Capitol+Records]Capitol[/url]. In 1973, Island's American division switched to independent distribution. US headquarters, formerly based in Los Angeles, were relocated to New York City in November 1977. In mid 1978, US Island began a series of manufacturing and distribution partnerships with major labels, first with [l=Warner Bros. Records Inc.], and then with [l=Atlantic Records] in late 1981. Similar relationships were forged with Philips [for the world except the US, UK and Australasia up to June 1971], Ariola [Europe from June 1971 except France], Festival [Australasia], Dacapo, and WEA for distribution in various other countries. For a history of relationships in Canada see [l280952].

Blackwell sold Island to PolyGram in 1989, but remained chairman of Island Entertainment Group until 1997. Since 1999, the Island label has been under the control of the [l=Island Def Jam Music Group] in the US and [l=Universal Island Records Ltd.] in the UK. In Germany, the brand is part of [l=Polydor Island Group], which formed from the short-lived [l=Island Mercury Labelgroup].  In Japan, the brand is used domestically by [l=Universal Sigma]. In November 2013, [a=Barry Weiss (3)] stepped down as Chairman/CEO of both Island and Def Jam. On the first day of April 2014, [l=Universal Music] dissolved The [l=Island Def Jam Music Group]. Now re-positioned Island Records, [l=Def Jam Recordings] and [l=Motown] separately as all three solo labels. In early 2024, Universal Music combined the operations of Island, Def Jam and [l=Republic Records] together under the unit name, [l=Republic Corps].
